content.text:
The `frontend-server` stage already runs the frontend through nginx and proxies `/api/` to the backend. Build that target explicitly—the default final stage, `binary`, only includes the backend:

```sh
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --target frontend-server -t exposed .
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env exposed
```

To put the server command in `CMD`, keep the existing entrypoint and change:

```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "/usr/local/bin/frontend-server"]
CMD ["exposed", "server"]
```

Then replace `exposed server &` in `docker/frontend-server.sh` with:

```bash
"$@" &
server_pid=$!
```

Keep the rest of the script unchanged. Docker passes `CMD` arguments to the wrapper, which starts the backend alongside nginx and handles shutdown. You can then override the command when running the container:

```sh
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env exposed exposed server
```
